items.q: Lumen Lighting plc has 40 million shares in issue. Its share price is 185p. What is its market capitalisation?
items.why: Market capitalisation = number of issued shares × current share price = 40 million × £1.85 = £74 million. Convert pence to pounds first: 185p is £1.85.
items.label: Calculate

items.q: Lumen Lighting plc paid a total dividend of £3.6 million. It has 45 million ordinary shares. What is the dividend per share?
items.why: Dividend per share = total dividend ÷ number of ordinary shares = £3,600,000 ÷ 45,000,000 = £0.08, which is 8p.
items.label: Calculate

items.q: A company pays a dividend of 8p per share. Its share price is 160p. What is the dividend yield?
items.why: Dividend yield = dividend per share (pence) ÷ share price (pence) × 100 = 8 ÷ 160 × 100 = 5%. 20% is the answer you get if you divide the wrong way round.
items.label: Calculate

items.q: The company's share price then falls from 160p to 128p and the dividend stays at 8p. What happens to the dividend yield?
opts: It rises to 25%, so the shares are now a very safe investment
It falls to 4%, because the business is now worth less
It stays at 5%, because the dividend has not changed
It rises to 6.25%, so each £1 invested now earns more dividend, although the fall in price may be a sign of problems
items.why: 8 ÷ 128 × 100 = 6.25%. A higher yield looks attractive, but the share price usually falls for a reason, such as lower expected profit, so the dividend may be cut later.
items.label: Use the answer

items.q: Firm A's sales are £12 million. The total market is worth £150 million. What is Firm A's market share?
items.why: Market share = sales of the business ÷ total sales in the market × 100 = 12 ÷ 150 × 100 = 8%.
items.label: Calculate

items.q: The market grows from £150 million to £168 million. What is the market growth?
items.why: Market growth = change in market size ÷ original market size × 100 = 18 ÷ 150 × 100 = 12%. Always divide by the original (older) figure.
items.label: Calculate

items.q: Over the same period Firm A's sales rise from £12 million to £13 million. What has happened to its market share?
opts: It has risen, because Firm A's sales went up
It has fallen, from 8% to about 7.7%, because the market grew faster than Firm A's sales
It has stayed at 8%, because both figures went up
items.why: 13 ÷ 168 × 100 = 7.7%. Firm A's sales grew by 8.3% but the market grew by 12%, so it lost share even though sales rose.
items.label: Use the answer

items.q: A business's sales rise from £2.4 million to £3.0 million. What is the percentage increase in sales?
items.why: Percentage change = change ÷ original × 100 = 0.6 ÷ 2.4 × 100 = 25%. 20% comes from dividing by the new figure.
items.label: Calculate

items.q: In a £200 million market, the three largest brands have sales of £36 million, £28 million and £18 million. What is their combined market share?
items.label: Calculate

items.q: What does a combined market share of 41% for the top three brands suggest?
opts: Each of the three brands has 41% of the market
There is no competition in the market
A few large firms have a big share, so a new business may find it hard to win customers from them
items.why: 41% shared between three brands means a few firms hold a large part of the market. They may have strong brands and bigger budgets, which makes entry harder, although 59% is still spread across smaller firms.
items.label: Use the answer

items.q: A business sells £4.5 million of goods, which is a 6% share of its market. What is the size of the market?
items.why: If 6% = £4.5 million, the whole market = 4.5 ÷ 0.06 = £75 million.
items.label: Calculate

items.q: A market sells 80,000 units a year. 35% of units are bought by under-25s. How many units does the under-25 segment buy?
items.label: Calculate

items.q: A business's sales were £5 million in 2022. Using 2022 as the base year (index = 100), its sales index for 2025 is 118. What were its sales in 2025?
items.why: An index of 118 means sales are 18% higher than in the base year. £5 million × 1.18 = £5.9 million.
items.label: Calculate

items.q: Over the same years, the market's index rose from 100 to 131. What does this tell you?
opts: The business's sales grew more slowly than the market, so its market share is likely to have fallen
The business grew faster than the market
items.why: The market grew by 31% but the business only grew by 18%, so it has probably lost market share.
items.label: Use the answer

items.q: A business surveys customers and finds 62% would buy a new product. The confidence interval at a 95% confidence level is ±5 percentage points. What is the range?
items.why: 62 − 5 = 57 and 62 + 5 = 67. The business can be 95% confident the true figure lies between 57% and 67%.
items.label: Calculate
